title: Relief Already Set Off Against a Ridgecrest Advantage Premium Account
content:
Credit adjustments already standing on the premium account of a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan enrollment are counted as relief already set off, and which of them are counted depends on the billing cadence of the enrollment and on whether any credit adjustment stands there at all.

| Where the account and the cadence show | The relief already set off |
| --- | --- |
| The enrollment is billed quarterly and at least 1 credit adjustment stands on the premium account | Every credit adjustment posted on the account in the contract year, whatever reason each of them carries |
| The enrollment is billed monthly and at least 1 credit adjustment stands on the premium account | The credit adjustments posted on the account in the last 3 months, whatever reason each of them carries |
| No credit adjustment stands on the premium account | Nothing |

The reason a credit adjustment carries makes no difference to whether it is counted: a credit granted for a billing error, for a duplicate payment, for a retroactive rate change or for a low income premium subsidy all count alike.

### Worked through on hypothetical figures

*An enrollment billed monthly with three credit adjustments standing on the account, of 20.00 USD and 15.00 USD posted in the last 3 months and 40.00 USD posted five months ago.* At least 1 credit adjustment stands there and the cadence is monthly, so the relief already set off is the two posted in the last 3 months, together 35.00 USD.

*The same three credit adjustments on an enrollment billed quarterly, all posted in the contract year.* At least 1 credit adjustment stands there and the cadence is quarterly, so the relief already set off is all three, together 75.00 USD.

*An enrollment with no credit adjustment standing on the premium account.* The relief already set off is nothing, whichever cadence the enrollment is billed on.
